title: Clairmont: Hamilton cop Ryan Tocher faces investigation again
subtitle: A Hamilton cop who has faced criminal and disciplinary charges in the past is once again under investigation.
article: A Hamilton cop who has faced criminal and disciplinary charges in the past is once again under investigation.

Ryan Tocher was exonerated when he killed two people and mistakenly beat another while on duty. Now he is being investigated by his own service in connection to a car that crashed into a hydro pole three months ago, leaving nearly 5,000 Binbrook residents without power, The Spectator has learned.

"There was an incident in which he was involved that is being investigated," says Tocher's lawyer, Gary Clewley, who has represented him in the past. No charges have been laid, according to Clewley, who says he has not seen the results of the investigation.
Police "have six months from the date of the incident" to lay a Police Services Act charge, he says.
Tocher, 38, is the only Hamilton cop to be investigated three times by the province's Special Investigations Unit.

In April 2007, Tocher shot and killed a 46-year-old Cambodian refugee named Soun Saing. Saing entered M&J Billiards on Parkdale Avenue North in the early morning and assaulted the owner. When police arrived they yelled at him to "Drop the axe," a coroner's inquest heard. Tocher and another officer fired after Saing lunged at them with a knife. He was hit by two bullets. The SIU cleared Tocher of any wrongdoing.
In May 2010, Tocher beat 58-year-old Myanmar native Po La Hay.
La Hay, a small man who speaks little English, was in his own home when police mistook his door for that of a drug dealer next door.

Not understanding what was happening, and already having a fear of police instilled while in Myanmar, La Hay did not quickly respond to commands. He was kicked and punched, suffering facial cuts and fractured ribs and vertebrae.
Tocher faced criminal charges laid by the SIU, but was found not guilty in court. His Police Services Act charges were dropped.
In February 2012, Tocher shot and killed Phonesay (Pun) Chanthachack, 27, from Laos.

Chanthachack was driving a stolen van and was boxed into a parking lot by unmarked police vans. He was already facing 18 charges, including break and enter, identity theft and credit-card theft. A warrant had been issued for his arrest after he failed to show up for court. Chanthachack drove at Tocher, who fired. Oddly, Chanthachack was shot in the back, a coroner's inquest heard.
Tocher was cleared of any wrongdoing by the SIU and went on to become a detective in the Homicide Unit.

When asked about the latest investigation involving Tocher, Hamilton police spokesperson Catherine Martin replied with an email: "If and when Police Services Act charges proceed to a First Appearance, there is a Police Services Act tribunal. The media is advised of all Police Services Act tribunals."
Tocher could not be reached for comment.
Police issued a media release following the crash, which happened Sept. 1, a Sunday, at about 1:45 a.m.
Officers were called to Highway 56 and Southbrook Road in Binbrook after a vehicle moving north on the highway left the road and hit a pole, the original release said.
"The impact of the collision caused a power outage lasting several hours in the Binbrook area," the release said.
It asked for anyone with information to call the Collision Reconstruction Unit.
The Spectator reported at the time that the crash left 4,750 homes in Binbrook, Glanford and Glanbrook without power.
We also reported that police said no one was injured in the crash.
